dataset.name: OSV vulnerability database records mirrored from GitHub-reviewed advisories
dataset.independent_adjudication: Each selected record has database_specific.github_reviewed=true; the advisory and affected-version ranges were published independently of FALSUM.

selection.candidate_rule: For each fixed package in the roster, retain GitHub-reviewed GHSA records with a numeric introduced/fixed interval; sort identifiers lexicographically and select the first two. No outcome-based case deletion or reselection is permitted.
selection.prior_roster_exclusion: No selected GHSA identifier appears in the existing FALSUM frozen source rosters or Phase 5BJ/5BL reports.
selection.case_construction: For each selected advisory, use one source-covered predecessor of the first fixed boundary and the exact fixed boundary. The predecessor is APPLICABLE and the fixed version is INAPPLICABLE according to the pinned source range.
selection.balance: 12 applicable and 12 inapplicable cases; each package contributes two of each; three PyPI and three npm package families are represented.

evaluation_contract.target_binding: Only the exact ecosystem, package and version in a generated case may be evaluated.
evaluation_contract.falsum_policy: Fail closed on withdrawn, mismatched, malformed or unsupported advisory evidence; use introduced/fixed/last_affected semantics.
evaluation_contract.competent_baseline: Independently implemented interval parser with the same source facts, exact package binding and explicit abstention on unsupported ranges; it does not call FALSUM helpers.
evaluation_contract.weaker_baseline: Citation-only policy that treats an exact package/advisory identifier as applicable without checking the version interval.
evaluation_contract.quality_discrimination: Compare each policy against the source-derived applicable/inapplicable label and report wins, ties and losses; do not infer exploitability or network ranking.
shortcut_audits: package-family leakage check against prior frozen rosters

limits: This is an unseen source-roster holdout for version applicability, not a human semantic AppSec gold set.
A GitHub-reviewed advisory is an independently published reference record, not proof of exploitability in an arbitrary deployment.
Agreement with the competent baseline is not a superiority claim.
No customer adoption, live Telegraph ranking change, maintainer acceptance or registered evaluator is inferred.
The benchmark is not used to train or tune FALSUM.
